Translate the accepted NL0 into a small, usable Lean interface and local
proof plan. Start with source-map.json and the problem/specification; read
individual NL0 definitions or paragraphs when needed. Yui translation rules
are available on demand. Do not read every rule or background note at startup.
The controller retains all accepted paragraphs and attaches each step's own
Audit A note index. Notes are optional implementation references, not new
premise ports: do not give every note a Lean type or add it to premise_types.
Mathematically reviewed background notes are mathematical assessments, not already verified Lean
declarations. Resolve concrete library bindings and auxiliary proof details
in this phase. Prepare public interfaces and genuinely shared definitions;
leave per-node tactic choices and local lemma searches to proof workers.
Do not front-load a complete Mathlib-use inventory into serial preparation.
Keep the original H/E project inputs and every N/P output. The pinned Mathlib
environment is freely available without registration. Prefer direct library use
to M premise ports; omit M roots unless an intermediate port is useful. Choose a
coherent Lean representation preserving domains, assumptions, quantifiers and
the full target. Definitions cannot hide unproved results or stronger assumptions.
Inspect the actual pinned declarations and the meanings of order/index and
capability parameters, including overloaded notation and coercions. Explain
their source meaning rather than relying on remembered symbol conventions.
Use typed steps for mathematical obligations; no proof bodies are required yet.

Submit an object with header, parameters, premise_types, conclusion_type,
representation, objects, steps, terminal, source_outputs, endpoint_correspondence.
endpoint_correspondence maps exactly every E ID and P to
{mode:direct|equivalent, explanation:<concise mathematical account>}. Explain
why each external statement and the WHOLE target (parameters, quantifiers,
hypotheses, conclusion) has the original meaning. Direct translations need only
a short account. For equivalent encodings, state the identification and why it
works in both directions under the actual assumptions. Do not invent a second
Lean representation just to prove an unnecessary conversion. If the proof
actually crosses two Lean representations, plan a checked conversion. These
notes are author guidance for the independent pre-freeze semantic review, not approval. header starts with
"import Mathlib
" and contains only object definitions/notation/structures,
no axioms, proof declarations, placeholders or executable metaprogramming.
parameters: [{name,type,binder_kind?}], where binder_kind is explicit (default),
implicit or instance. premise_types maps every H/E root and any retained M
port to its Lean proposition. Mathlib references are not a permission list. source_outputs maps every N/P to a distinct step Tddd. steps:
[{id,statement,inputs:[root/T IDs],source_steps:[S IDs],explanation}]. Each step
is a closed conditional obligation; include useful independent subarguments or
representation bridges when they reduce work. Every step must reach terminal;
cover all source paragraphs. terminal's type equals conclusion_type. objects
may be [] when special representation views are unnecessary. representation
explains the chosen encoding; it is not a semantic approval.

Save incomplete work with save_interface_draft; revise it with base_candidate
and explicit JSON-pointer patches. Use check_lean_types for uncertain APIs or
small type fragments, and check_draft when the full interface is ready. A full
check runs real Lean type elaboration and source-boundary checks. Continue from
your saved candidate after errors. Do not stop just to report ordinary progress.
At author acceptance, a separate semantic interface reviewer checks source
correspondence before proof workers start. Final Audit B independently checks semantic
faithfulness and the assembled proof. A type check is never a semantic PASS.

Read the stage rules on demand; no need to preload the whole skill. Relevant frozen rule paths (relative to the installed skill root): nl02lean/references/minimal-translation.md. Other declared Markdown references linked from these remain available through read_yui. Reads return explicit pages of at most 250 lines with continuation metadata. Follow relevant links; operator scheduling/control manuals are not proof-worker inputs.
Frozen task document IDs: background-supplement.json, nl0.json, problem.md, source-map.json, spec.json, target-selection.json. Use read_task_input to read them.
Prefer check_draft/submit_draft with an actual artifact JSON object. The older check_artifact/submit_artifact wrappers require artifact_json to be a double-encoded valid JSON string; do not supply Python dictionaries or single-quoted keys. Both forms run identical checks.
You may revise an explicit pre-freeze prior-interface.json through {"base_input":"prior-interface.json","patches":[{"op":"replace","path":"/header","value":"complete replacement header"}]}. The result is fully expanded and checked; this never supplies missing mathematics. After a full candidate exists, preserve it with base_candidate:N and explicit patches, or submit {"accept_candidate":N} only when that actual candidate is complete and faithful. read_interface_draft kind=index lists your own actual full candidates and partial type probes; kind=candidate reads a JSON pointer of a full candidate, kind=probe reads its own actual partial header/types. After context reset, inspect this index rather than starting from a vacuous True template. A placeholder is not a translation. Choose useful closed obligations; a large worker limit cannot accelerate a monolithic job. Optional shared_obligations must use the existing v2 schema and describe only existing NL0 lemmas or implementation extraction, with explicit inputs and route. They remain pending actual semantic review; new mathematics returns to NL0.

{"id": "source-map.json", "pointer": "", "view": "value", "value": {"background_mode": "node_local_reference", "source_steps": [{"id": "S001", "text": "Fix m, A and s as declared. Apply M001 to the Euclidean metric space R^m, its Borel measurable structure, exponent s and set A. At each finite positive scale, the formula's covers are exactly the covers in D002: a countable family can be enumerated by natural numbers, padding with empty sets if finite, and conversely a sequence is countable. All nonempty sets allowed at such a scale are bounded, so their extended diameters equal their ordinary finite Euclidean diameters. Empty members have cost zero in both definitions; since s>0, nonempty singletons also have zero cost. Thus the inner infimum is exactly the supplied scale content. The extra scale infinity in M001 adds nothing to the supremum: its admissible covers include all covers at scale 1, so its infimum is at most the scale-1 content. The finite positive extended scales are precisely the positive real scales. Taking their supremum proves F001: H^s(A)=μH[s](A). No dimensional normalization constant is introduced."}, {"id": "S002", "text": "Use F001 to transport the four critical-exponent facts. Under L1: 0<s<dim_H(A), M002 with nonnegative exponent a=s gives μH[s](A)=infinity, hence H^s(A)=infinity; discharge L1. Under L2: dim_H(A)<s, M003 gives μH[s](A)=0, hence H^s(A)=0; discharge L2. Under L3: H^s(A)=0, F001 makes μH[s](A)=0≠infinity, and M004 gives dim_H(A)≤s; discharge L3. Under L4: H^s(A)=infinity, F001 and M005 give s≤dim_H(A); discharge L4. These are the complete conditional assertions F002."}, {"id": "S003", "text": "The dimension in D004 is a supremum in the nonnegative extended reals, so it is nonnegative, including for the empty set. The arbitrary choices of m,A,s and F001-F002 prove every clause of the output proposition."}, {"id": "S004", "text": "By H003, E is compact, hence bounded in its Euclidean metric. A bounded subset of R^n is contained in a coordinate box [-b,b]^n for some b>0: each coordinate distance is at most the Euclidean distance, and increasing a bound if necessary makes it positive. This also holds in R^0. Record F001. H001 specifies the nonnegative ambient dimension; N001 gives D≥0."}, {"id": "S005", "text": "Choose b from F001 and define C as declared. Under L1: n>0, fix arbitrary a and h under L2: a>n and L3: 0<h≤1. Divide each coordinate interval [-b,b] into ceil(2b/h) intervals of side at most h. Their number is at most (2b+1)/h in each coordinate, hence the resulting at most C h^(-n) closed cubes cover E. Each cube has Euclidean diameter at most sqrt(n)h. Therefore their total a-cost is at most C h^(-n)(sqrt(n)h)^a=C n^(a/2)h^(a-n). Since a-n>0, this tends to zero as h decreases to zero, and their diameters also tend to zero. In particular, at each fixed target scale arbitrarily small h provides admissible covers with costs tending to zero, so H^a(E)=0. Discharge L3 after using the arbitrary mesh sizes. N001 with A=E, exponent a gives D≤a. Since a>n was arbitrary, D≤n (if D>n, choose a strictly between n and D). Discharge L2 and L1. This proves F002."}, {"id": "S006", "text": "Under L4: n=0, Euclidean R^0 consists of its single empty-coordinate point. H002 implies E=R^0. A cover by that singleton has diameter and s-cost zero for every positive exponent s. Thus H^s(E)=0 for all s>0, and N001 gives D≤s for every s>0, whence D=0 using D≥0. Discharge L4. By H001 the alternatives n=0 and n>0 exhaust the ambient dimensions. F002 and this branch give 0≤D≤n, so D is finite, with the stated singleton conclusion when n=0."}, {"id": "S007", "text": "Fix arbitrary positive s and delta. The open balls of radius delta/2 centered at the points of E form an open cover. By H003 there is a finite subcover, and each such ball has diameter at most delta. Its finite number of members and finite diameters give a finite total s-cost. The defining infimum therefore gives H^s_delta(E)<infinity. Together with F003 this proves the output proposition."}, {"id": "S008", "text": "Fix arbitrary a under L1: a>1. For each positive integer N, divide I into N closed intervals of length 1/N. They have total a-cost N(1/N)^a=N^(1-a), which tends to zero as N tends to infinity, while their maximum diameter tends to zero. Thus at every positive target scale the defining infimum is zero, and H^a(I)=0. N001 applied with ambient dimension 1 gives dim_H(I)≤a; taking a down to 1 gives dim_H(I)≤1. Discharge L1 and record F001, including the universally quantified zero-measure assertion."}, {"id": "S009", "text": "Fix delta>0 and an arbitrary sequence V under L2: V is a delta-cover of I. Define rho as declared; each rho_i≤delta is finite. Fix epsilon>0 and define J as declared. A nonempty V_i is bounded, so its real supremum and infimum exist and sup(V_i)-inf(V_i)=rho_i. Therefore V_i⊆J_i and |J_i|≤rho_i+epsilon*2^(-i-1), also when V_i is empty. The open sets J_i cover I. Countable subadditivity of Lebesgue measure and |I|=1 give 1≤sum_i |J_i|≤sum_i rho_i+epsilon, using sum_{i≥0}2^(-i-1)=1. If sum_i rho_i is infinite the required inequality is immediate; if finite, letting the arbitrary epsilon decrease to zero yields F002: sum_i rho_i≥1. All sets measured here are open intervals or I, so no measurability of V_i is assumed."}, {"id": "S010", "text": "Fix arbitrary s under L3: 0<s<1. For each i with rho_i>0, rho_i≤delta and s-1<0 give rho_i^s=rho_i*rho_i^(s-1)≥delta^(s-1)*rho_i. The inequality also holds when rho_i=0 since s>0. Summing nonnegative terms and using F002 gives sum_i rho_i^s≥delta^(s-1)sum_i rho_i≥delta^(s-1). Since V was an arbitrary delta-cover, taking the infimum gives H^s_delta(I)≥delta^(s-1). Discharge L2 in this universal cover conclusion. Since delta>0 was arbitrary and delta^(s-1) tends to infinity as delta decreases to zero, H^s(I)=infinity. N001 gives dim_H(I)≥s. Let s increase to 1 to get dim_H(I)≥1, and discharge L3. Together with F001 this is dim_H(I)=1 and all the measure assertions of the output proposition."}, {"id": "S011", "text": "Under L1: n=0, N002 gives E=R^0 and D=0. The coordinate map from I to F obtained by adjoining the unique R^0 coordinate preserves all distances. Fix arbitrary a under L4: a>1. N003 gives H^a(I)=0, so by the defining infimum there are covers of I at every positive scale with arbitrarily small a-cost. Push these covers forward by that coordinate map; their diameters are unchanged, so H^a(F)=0. N001 gives dim_H(F)≤a. Let the arbitrary a decrease to 1 to obtain dim_H(F)≤1=D+1. Discharge L4 and L1 and record F000."}, {"id": "S012", "text": "For the other branch introduce L2: n≥1. Fix arbitrary q under L3: q>D, and arbitrary positive delta and epsilon. N002 gives D≥0, so q>0. Define r=min(1,delta/sqrt(2))>0; thus r≤1 and sqrt(2)r≤delta. By N001 applied to E, H^q(E)=0. The nonnegative content H^q_r(E) is at most this supremum, hence zero. The infimum defining that content therefore supplies a countable r-cover W with total q-cost<epsilon/2. The infimum is zero, so its admissible family is nonempty (an empty infimum is infinity); its defining approximation property gives the stated cover. Nonempty positive-diameter members are unchanged; every point originally covered remains covered. The additional cost is at most sum_{i≥0}epsilon*2^(-i-3)=epsilon/4<epsilon/2. Thus, after discarding empty members by restricting to K, U is a countable cover of E with 0<r_i≤r and sum_{i∈K}r_i^q<epsilon. This is F002; the countable index set may be finite."}, {"id": "S014", "text": "For i∈K define N_i=ceil(1/r_i). Divide I into N_i closed intervals, each of length 1/N_i≤r_i. sum_(i∈K) N_i (sqrt(2)r_i)^(q+1)
≤2(sqrt(2))^(q+1) sum_(i∈K) r_i^q
<2(sqrt(2))^(q+1)epsilon.
These inequalities follow termwise from N_i≤2/r_i and then by nonnegative summation, so they remain valid for countably many members. Since delta>0 was arbitrary, H^(q+1)(F)=0. N001, with ambient dimension n+1 and positive exponent q+1, gives dim_H(F)≤q+1. Since q>D was arbitrary and D is finite by N002, let q decrease to D to obtain dim_H(F)≤D+1: an alleged strict excess would allow a q between D and dim_H(F)-1, contradicting this bound (an infinite dimension is already excluded by any one q>D). This is F004."}, {"id": "S021", "text": "If sum_i rho_i^(s+1)=infinity, c≤sum_i rho_i^(s+1) holds immediately. {"id": "problem.md", "total_lines": 175, "start": 1, "end": 175, "start_column": 0, "end_column": 65, "requested_end": 200, "has_more": false, "next_start": null, "next_column": 0, "next_end": null, "text": "1: # Hausdorff dimension of a product with an interval
2: 
3: ## Original exercise
4: 
5: Elias M. Stein and Rami Shakarchi, *Real Analysis: Measure Theory,
6: Integration, and Hilbert Spaces*, Princeton Lectures in Analysis III,
7: Chapter 7, Problems, exercise 9, printed page 388.
8: Book DOI: [10.1515/9781400835560](https://doi.org/10.1515/9781400835560).
9: 
10: > 9. Let \(E\) be a compact set in \(\mathbb R^{d-1}\). Show that
11: > \(\dim(E\times I)=\dim(E)+1\), where \(I\) is the unit interval in
12: > \(\mathbb R\).
13: 
14: ## Fixed interpretation and complete target
15: 
16: Here dimension means **Hausdorff dimension**. As approved by the user on
17: 2026-10-23, assume explicitly that \(E\) is nonempty. With the convention
18: \(\dim_H\varnothing=0\), the printed equality would otherwise fail for
19: the empty set. This is a disclosed addition to the printed exercise.
20: 
21: Let \(n\geq0\) be an integer, let \(E\subset\mathbb R^n\) be a nonempty
22: compact set, and put \(I=[0,1]\). Identify \(\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R\)
23: with \(\mathbb R^{n+1}\) and use its Euclidean metric. Prove
24: 
25: \[
26: \dim_H(E\times[0,1])=\dim_H E+1.
27: \]
28: 
29: The zero-dimensional ambient space \(\mathbb R^0\) is included. A later
30: formalization using a different product norm must justify the metric change.
31: 
32: ## Fixed natural-language proof
33: 
34: For a Euclidean set \(A\), exponent \(s>0\), and scale \(\delta>0\), put
35: 
36: \[
37: H^s_\delta(A)=\inf\left\{\sum_i(\operatorname{diam}U_i)^s:
38:  A\subseteq\bigcup_iU_i,\quad\operatorname{diam}U_i\leq\delta\right\},
39: \qquad H^s(A)=\sup_{\delta>0}H^s_\delta(A).
40: \]
41: 
42: Covers are countable, with empty members contributing zero. This
43: unnormalized Hausdorff measure gives the usual Hausdorff dimension. We use
44: its critical-exponent characterization: \(H^s(A)=0\) if
45: \(s>\dim_H A\), and \(H^s(A)=\infty\) if \(0<s<\dim_H A\).
46: Conversely, zero measure implies \(\dim_H A\leq s\), and infinite
47: measure implies \(\dim_H A\geq s\).
48: 
49: Write \(D=\dim_H E\) and \(F=E\times[0,1]\). First \(0\leq D\leq n\).
50: Indeed, compactness makes \(E\) bounded. When \(n>0\), a box containing
51: it admits a cover by at most \(Ch^{-n}\) cubes of side at most \(h\),
52: for \(0<h\leq1\). Here \(C\) depends only on that box. Each cube has
53: diameter at most \(\sqrt n h\). For any \(s>n\), the total \(s\)-cost
54: is at most \(C n^{s/2}h^{s-n}\to0\). These arbitrarily fine covers
55: give \(H^s(E)=0\) and hence \(D\leq n\). If \(n=0\), nonemptiness
56: makes \(E=\mathbb R^0\), a singleton of zero \(s\)-cost for every
57: \(s>0\); thus \(D=0\).
58: 
59: ### Upper bound
60: 
61: When \(n=0\), \(F\) is isometric to \([0,1]\). Dividing this interval
62: into \(N\) equal pieces gives total \(a\)-cost \(N^{1-a}\to0\) for
63: every \(a>1\), proving \(\dim_H F\leq1=D+1\).
64: For this upper-bound argument now assume \(n\geq1\).
65: 
66: Fix \(q>D\). Since \(q>0\) and \(H^q(E)=0\), for every
67: \(0<r\leq1\) and \(\varepsilon>0\) there is a countable cover
68: \((U_i)\) of \(E\) with nonempty-member diameters
69: \(0<r_i\leq r\) and \(\sum_i r_i^q<\varepsilon\).
70: The positive-diameter requirement costs nothing: start with a cover of
71: cost below \(\varepsilon/2\); replace each zero-diameter singleton by
72: a ball of diameter at most \(r\), choosing the \(i\)-th replacement
73: to have \(q\)-cost less than \(\varepsilon2^{-i-2}\). The added cost
74: is less than \(\varepsilon/2\). Discard empty members.
75: 
76: Let \(N_i=\lceil1/r_i\rceil\). Partition \([0,1]\) into \(N_i\)
77: closed intervals of length \(1/N_i\leq r_i\). Because \(r_i\leq1\),
78: \(N_i\leq2/r_i\). The corresponding products with \(U_i\) form a
79: countable cover of \(F\). Each has Euclidean diameter at most
80: \(\sqrt2 r_i\), and their total \((q+1)\)-cost is at most
81: 
82: \[
83: \sum_iN_i(\sqrt2 r_i)^{q+1}
84: \leq2(\sqrt2)^{q+1}\sum_i r_i^q
85: <2(\sqrt2)^{q+1}\varepsilon.
86: \]
87: 
88: For any target scale \(\delta>0\), choose
89: \(r\leq\min(1,\delta/\sqrt2)\), then let \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\).
90: Thus \(H^{q+1}_\delta(F)=0\) for every scale, so
91: \(H^{q+1}(F)=0\) and \(\dim_H F\leq q+1\). Letting \(q\downarrow D\)
92: gives \(\dim_H F\leq D+1\).
93: 
94: ### Lower bound when \(D>0\)
95: 
96: Fix \(0<s<D\). Then \(H^s(E)=\infty\), so
97: \(H^s_\delta(E)\) becomes arbitrarily large as \(\delta\downarrow0\).
98: We claim that, for every \(\delta>0\),
99: 
100: \[
101: H^s_\delta(E)\leq H^{s+1}_\delta(F).                 \tag{1}
102: \]
103: 
104: Take an arbitrary countable \(\delta\)-cover \((V_i)_{i\geq0}\) of
105: \(F\), discarding empty members. Define
106: \(\rho_i=\operatorname{diam}V_i\),
107: \(A_i=\pi_{\mathbb R^n}(V_i)\), and
108: \(B_i=\pi_{\mathbb R}(V_i)\). Coordinate projections are 1-Lipschitz,

{"id": "problem.md", "total_lines": 175, "start": 1, "end": 175, "start_column": 0, "end_column": 65, "requested_end": 200, "has_more": false, "next_start": null, "next_column": 0, "next_end": null, "text": "1: # Hausdorff dimension of a product with an interval
2: 
3: ## Original exercise
4: 
5: Elias M. Stein and Rami Shakarchi, *Real Analysis: Measure Theory,
6: Integration, and Hilbert Spaces*, Princeton Lectures in Analysis III,
7: Chapter 7, Problems, exercise 9, printed page 388.
8: Book DOI: [10.1515/9781400835560](https://doi.org/10.1515/9781400835560).
9: 
10: > 9. Let \(E\) be a compact set in \(\mathbb R^{d-1}\). Show that
11: > \(\dim(E\times I)=\dim(E)+1\), where \(I\) is the unit interval in
12: > \(\mathbb R\).
13: 
14: ## Fixed interpretation and complete target
15: 
16: Here dimension means **Hausdorff dimension**. As approved by the user on
17: 2026-10-23, assume explicitly that \(E\) is nonempty. With the convention
18: \(\dim_H\varnothing=0\), the printed equality would otherwise fail for
19: the empty set. This is a disclosed addition to the printed exercise.
20: 
21: Let \(n\geq0\) be an integer, let \(E\subset\mathbb R^n\) be a nonempty
22: compact set, and put \(I=[0,1]\). Identify \(\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R\)
23: with \(\mathbb R^{n+1}\) and use its Euclidean metric. Prove
24: 
25: \[
26: \dim_H(E\times[0,1])=\dim_H E+1.
27: \]
28: 
29: The zero-dimensional ambient space \(\mathbb R^0\) is included. A later
30: formalization using a different product norm must justify the metric change.
31: 
32: ## Fixed natural-language proof
33: 
34: For a Euclidean set \(A\), exponent \(s>0\), and scale \(\delta>0\), put
35: 
36: \[
37: H^s_\delta(A)=\inf\left\{\sum_i(\operatorname{diam}U_i)^s:
38:  A\subseteq\bigcup_iU_i,\quad\operatorname{diam}U_i\leq\delta\right\},
39: \qquad H^s(A)=\sup_{\delta>0}H^s_\delta(A).
40: \]
41: 
42: Covers are countable, with empty members contributing zero. This
43: unnormalized Hausdorff measure gives the usual Hausdorff dimension. We use
44: its critical-exponent characterization: \(H^s(A)=0\) if
45: \(s>\dim_H A\), and \(H^s(A)=\infty\) if \(0<s<\dim_H A\).
46: Conversely, zero measure implies \(\dim_H A\leq s\), and infinite
47: measure implies \(\dim_H A\geq s\).
48: 
49: Write \(D=\dim_H E\) and \(F=E\times[0,1]\). First \(0\leq D\leq n\).
50: Indeed, compactness makes \(E\) bounded. When \(n>0\), a box containing
51: it admits a cover by at most \(Ch^{-n}\) cubes of side at most \(h\),
52: for \(0<h\leq1\). Here \(C\) depends only on that box. Each cube has
53: diameter at most \(\sqrt n h\). For any \(s>n\), the total \(s\)-cost
54: is at most \(C n^{s/2}h^{s-n}\to0\). These arbitrarily fine covers
55: give \(H^s(E)=0\) and hence \(D\leq n\). If \(n=0\), nonemptiness
56: makes \(E=\mathbb R^0\), a singleton of zero \(s\)-cost for every
57: \(s>0\); thus \(D=0\).
58: 
59: ### Upper bound
60: 
61: When \(n=0\), \(F\) is isometric to \([0,1]\). Dividing this interval
62: into \(N\) equal pieces gives total \(a\)-cost \(N^{1-a}\to0\) for
63: every \(a>1\), proving \(\dim_H F\leq1=D+1\).
64: For this upper-bound argument now assume \(n\geq1\).
65: 
66: Fix \(q>D\). Since \(q>0\) and \(H^q(E)=0\), for every
67: \(0<r\leq1\) and \(\varepsilon>0\) there is a countable cover
68: \((U_i)\) of \(E\) with nonempty-member diameters
69: \(0<r_i\leq r\) and \(\sum_i r_i^q<\varepsilon\).
70: The positive-diameter requirement costs nothing: start with a cover of
71: cost below \(\varepsilon/2\); replace each zero-diameter singleton by
72: a ball of diameter at most \(r\), choosing the \(i\)-th replacement
73: to have \(q\)-cost less than \(\varepsilon2^{-i-2}\). The added cost
74: is less than \(\varepsilon/2\). Discard empty members.
75: 
76: Let \(N_i=\lceil1/r_i\rceil\). Partition \([0,1]\) into \(N_i\)
77: closed intervals of length \(1/N_i\leq r_i\). Because \(r_i\leq1\),
78: \(N_i\leq2/r_i\). The corresponding products with \(U_i\) form a
79: countable cover of \(F\). Each has Euclidean diameter at most
80: \(\sqrt2 r_i\), and their total \((q+1)\)-cost is at most
81: 
82: \[
83: \sum_iN_i(\sqrt2 r_i)^{q+1}
84: \leq2(\sqrt2)^{q+1}\sum_i r_i^q
85: <2(\sqrt2)^{q+1}\varepsilon.
86: \]
87: 
88: For any target scale \(\delta>0\), choose
89: \(r\leq\min(1,\delta/\sqrt2)\), then let \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\).
90: Thus \(H^{q+1}_\delta(F)=0\) for every scale, so
91: \(H^{q+1}(F)=0\) and \(\dim_H F\leq q+1\). Letting \(q\downarrow D\)
92: gives \(\dim_H F\leq D+1\).
93: 
94: ### Lower bound when \(D>0\)
95: 
96: Fix \(0<s<D\). Then \(H^s(E)=\infty\), so
97: \(H^s_\delta(E)\) becomes arbitrarily large as \(\delta\downarrow0\).
98: We claim that, for every \(\delta>0\),
99: 
100: \[
101: H^s_\delta(E)\leq H^{s+1}_\delta(F).                 \tag{1}
102: \]
103: 
104: Take an arbitrary countable \(\delta\)-cover \((V_i)_{i\geq0}\) of
105: \(F\), discarding empty members. Define
106: \(\rho_i=\operatorname{diam}V_i\),
107: \(A_i=\pi_{\mathbb R^n}(V_i)\), and
108: \(B_i=\pi_{\mathbb R}(V_i)\). Coordinate projections are 1-Lipschitz,
109: so both projected diameters are at most \(\rho_i\leq\delta\).
110: For \(\varepsilon>0\), put
111: 
112: \[
113: \eta_i=\frac{\varepsilon2^{-i-1}}{1+\rho_i^s}>0.
114: \]
115: 
116: Enclose \(B_i\) in an open interval \(J_i\) of length at most
117: \(\rho_i+\eta_i\): its supremum minus infimum is at most \(\rho_i\),
118: and an enlargement of total width \(\eta_i\) suffices. This avoids
119: assuming that the arbitrary covering sets or their projections are measurable.
120: 
121: For each \(t\in[0,1]\), the sets \(A_i\) for which \(t\in J_i\)
122: cover \(E\). Indeed, a point \((x,t)\in F\) belongs to some \(V_i\),
123: giving \(x\in A_i\) and \(t\in B_i\subset J_i\). Their diameters
124: are at most \(\rho_i\). Consequently, with \(c=H^s_\delta(E)\),
125: 
126: \[
127: c\leq\sum_i\rho_i^s\mathbf1_{J_i}(t)\quad(t\in[0,1]).
128: \]
129: 
130: The constant \(c\) is finite: compactness gives a finite cover of \(E\)
131: by balls of diameter at most \(\delta\), with finite \(s\)-cost.
132: Each summand is nonnegative and measurable since \(J_i\) is open.
133: Integrate over \([0,1]\), of Lebesgue measure one, and use Tonelli's
134: theorem for this nonnegative series. Since
135: \(|J_i\cap[0,1]|\leq\rho_i+\eta_i\),
136: 
137: \[
138: \begin{aligned}
139: c&\leq\sum_i\rho_i^s|J_i\cap[0,1]|\\
140:  &\leq\sum_i\rho_i^{s+1}+\sum_i\eta_i\rho_i^s
141:  \leq\sum_i\rho_i^{s+1}+\varepsilon.
142: \end{aligned}
143: \]
144: 
145: If the first series is infinite the desired inequality is immediate;
146: otherwise let \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\). Take the infimum over the
147: arbitrary covers to obtain (1). As its left side is unbounded at small
148: scales, \(H^{s+1}(F)=\infty\), giving \(\dim_H F\geq s+1\).
149: Letting \(s\uparrow D\) proves \(\dim_H F\geq D+1\).
150: 
151: ### Lower bound when \(D=0\)
152: 
153: Choose \(x_0\in E\). The map \(t\mapsto(x_0,t)\) is an isometric
154: embedding of \([0,1]\) into \(F\), so dimension monotonicity gives
155: \(\dim_H F\geq\dim_H[0,1]\). This interval has dimension one:
156: equal-length covers gave the upper bound above. For \(0<s<1\), any
157: \(\delta\)-cover with diameters \(\rho_i\leq\delta\) satisfies
158: \(\sum_i\rho_i\geq1\). To see this, enclose its nonempty members
159: in open intervals of lengths at most \(\rho_i+\varepsilon2^{-i-1}\),
160: use countable subadditivity of length to get
161: \(1\leq\sum_i\rho_i+\varepsilon\), and let \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\).
162: Hence \(\sum_i\rho_i^s\geq\delta^{s-1}\sum_i\rho_i
163: \geq\delta^{s-1}\to\infty\) as \(\delta\downarrow0\).
164: This proves the lower bound one. Thus \(\dim_H F\geq1=D+1\),
165: including when \(n=0\).
166: 
167: Together the bounds establish the required equality.
168: 
169: ## Input status
170: 
171: This file fixes the problem, conventions and supplied proof route for future
172: tests. It is a natural-language input, not an NL0 artifact, an Audit A receipt,
173: a Lean proof, or a passing test result. Future runs must independently produce
174: and check those artifacts. The basic Hausdorff-measure and integration facts
175: used here must be registered by that future NL0/Audit A workflow."}

{"id": "spec.json", "pointer": "", "view": "value", "value": {"format_version": 2, "case_id": "geometry-product-dimension", "full_target": "# Hausdorff dimension of a product with an interval

## Original exercise

Elias M. Stein and Rami Shakarchi, *Real Analysis: Measure Theory,
Integration, and Hilbert Spaces*, Princeton Lectures in Analysis III,
Chapter 7, Problems, exercise 9, printed page 388.
Book DOI: [10.1515/9781400835560](https://doi.org/10.1515/9781400835560).

> 9. Let \(E\) be a compact set in \(\mathbb R^{d-1}\). Show that
> \(\dim(E\times I)=\dim(E)+1\), where \(I\) is the unit interval in
> \(\mathbb R\).

## Fixed interpretation and complete target

Here dimension means **Hausdorff dimension**. As approved by the user on
2026-10-23, assume explicitly that \(E\) is nonempty. With the convention
\(\dim_H\varnothing=0\), the printed equality would otherwise fail for
the empty set. This is a disclosed addition to the printed exercise.

Let \(n\geq0\) be an integer, let \(E\subset\mathbb R^n\) be a nonempty
compact set, and put \(I=[0,1]\). Identify \(\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R\)
with \(\mathbb R^{n+1}\) and use its Euclidean metric. Prove

\[
\dim_H(E\times[0,1])=\dim_H E+1.
\]

The zero-dimensional ambient space \(\mathbb R^0\) is included. A later
formalization using a different product norm must justify the metric change.", "conclusion": "dim_H(E×[0,1])=dim_H(E)+1, with R^n×R identified with Euclidean R^(n+1), including n=0.", "parameters": [{"symbol": "n", "type": "natural number (encoding the original nonnegative integer)"}, {"symbol": "E", "type": "subset of Euclidean R^n"}], "hypotheses": [{"id": "H001", "statement": "n≥0.", "origin": "problem.md:21; the original nonnegative integer is represented by a natural number."}, {"id": "H002", "statement": "E is nonempty.", "origin": "problem.md:16-22; explicitly approved addition to the printed exercise."}, {"id": "H003", "statement": "E is compact in Euclidean R^n.", "origin": "problem.md:21-23"}], "definitions": [{"id": "D001", "symbol": "diam", "type": "extended nonnegative diameter of a subset of a metric or extended metric space", "definition": "For a subset A of a metric or extended metric space X, diam(A)=sup{dist(x,y):x,y in A}, using extended distance and sup(empty)=0. \[
H^s_\delta(A)=\inf\left\{\sum_i(\operatorname{diam}U_i)^s:
 A\subseteq\bigcup_iU_i,\quad\operatorname{diam}U_i\leq\delta\right\},
\qquad H^s(A)=\sup_{\delta>0}H^s_\delta(A).
\]

Covers are countable, with empty members contributing zero. This
unnormalized Hausdorff measure gives the usual Hausdorff dimension.

26: 
27: * `WithLp p V`: a copy of `V` to be equipped with an L`p` norm.
28: * `WithLp.toLp`: the canonical inclusion from `V` to `WithLp p V`.
29: * `WithLp.ofLp`: the canonical inclusion from `WithLp p V` to `V`.
30: * `WithLp.linearEquiv p K V`: the canonical `K`-module isomorphism between `WithLp p V` and `V`.
31: 
32: ## Implementation notes
33: 
34: The pattern here is the same one as is used by `Lex` for order structures; it avoids having a
35: separate synonym for each type (`ProdLp`, `PiLp`, etc), and allows all the structure-copying code
36: to be shared.
37: 
38: TODO: is it safe to copy across the topology and uniform space structure too for all reasonable
39: choices of `V`?
40: -/
41: 
42: @[expose] public section
43: 
44: 
45: open scoped ENNReal
46: 
47: /-- A type synonym for the given `V`, associated with the L`p` norm. Note that by default this just
48: forgets the norm structure on `V`; it is up to downstream users to implement the L`p` norm (for
49: instance, on `Prod` and finite `Pi` types). -/
50: structure WithLp (p : ℝ≥0∞) (V : Type*) where
51:   /-- Converts an element of `V` to an element of `WithLp p V`. -/
52:   toLp (p) ::
53:   /-- Converts an element of `WithLp p V` to an element of `V`. -/
54:   ofLp : V
55: 
56: section Notation
57: 
58: open Lean.PrettyPrinter.Delaborator
59: 
60: /-- This prevents `toLp p x` being printed as `{ ofLp := x }` by `delabStructureInstance`. -/
61: @[app_delab WithLp.toLp]
62: meta def WithLp.delabToLp : Delab := delabApp
63: 
64: end Notation
65: 
66: variable (p : ℝ≥0∞) (K K' : Type*) {K'' : Type*} (V : Type*) {V' V'' : Type*}
67: 
68: namespace WithLp
69: 
70: /-- `WithLp.ofLp` and `WithLp.toLp` as an equivalence. -/
71: @[simps]
72: protected def equiv : WithLp p V ≃ V where
73:   toFun := ofLp
74:   invFun := toLp p
75:   left_inv _ := rfl
76:   right_inv _ := rfl
77: 
78: @[simp]
79: lemma equiv_symm_apply : ⇑(WithLp.equiv p V).symm = toLp p := rfl
80: 
81: /-! `WithLp p V` inherits various module-adjacent structures from `V`. -/
82: 
83: instance instNontrivial [Nontrivial V] : Nontrivial (WithLp p V) := (WithLp.equiv p V).nontrivial
84: instance instUnique [Unique V] : Unique (WithLp p V) := (WithLp.equiv p V).unique"}

505: def snoc (p : ∀ i : Fin n, α i.castSucc) (x : α (last n)) (i : Fin (n + 1)) : α i :=
506:   if h : i.val < n then _root_.cast (by rw [Fin.castSucc_castLT i h]) (p (castLT i h))
507:   else _root_.cast (by rw [eq_last_of_not_lt h]) x

import Mathlib
open scoped ENNReal NNReal
namespace GP
abbrev Space (n : ℕ) := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)
def unitInterval : Set ℝ := Set.Icc 0 1
def join {n : ℕ} (x : Space n) (t : ℝ) : Space (n + 1) :=
  WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.snoc (fun i => x i) t)
def horizontal {n : ℕ} (z : Space (n + 1)) : Space n :=
  WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => z i.castSucc)
def vertical {n : ℕ} (z : Space (n + 1)) : ℝ := z (Fin.last n)
def cylinder {n : ℕ} (E : Set (Space n)) : Set (Space (n + 1)) :=
  {z | horizontal z ∈ E ∧ vertical z ∈ unitInterval}
def Cover {X : Type*} [EMetricSpace X] (A : Set X) (δ : ℝ)
    (U : ℕ → Set X) : Prop :=
  A ⊆ ⋃ i, U i ∧ ∀ i, Metric.ediam (U i) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal δ
noncomputable def cost {X : Type*} [EMetricSpace X] (s : ℝ)
    (U : ℕ → Set X) : ℝ≥0∞ :=
  ∑' i, ⨆ (_ : (U i).Nonempty), (Metric.ediam (U i)) ^ s
noncomputable def content {X : Type*} [EMetricSpace X] (s δ : ℝ)
    (A : Set X) : ℝ≥0∞ :=
  ⨅ (U : ℕ → Set X) (_ : Cover A δ U), cost s U
noncomputable def hausdorff {X : Type*} [EMetricSpace X] (s : ℝ)
    (A : Set X) : ℝ≥0∞ :=
  ⨆ (δ : ℝ) (_ : 0 < δ), content s δ A
end GP
